items.title: AI agents hit the software supply chain
items.oneliner: RubyGems says AI agents pushed 2,000 malicious packages. Package registries now need bot defenses, not just malware scanning.

items.title: Anthropic publicly calls for slower frontier scaling
items.oneliner: Dario Amodei says self-improving AI could outrun oversight. Safety is becoming a product and policy constraint.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra reduces coding babysitting
items.oneliner: A 150,000-line app reportedly migrated with far less debugging on GPT-6 Astra. Reliability is becoming the real benchmark.

items.title: Google makes search scraping materially harder
items.oneliner: Google's new google.com/goto redirects hide result URLs. Training-data collection just got slower, pricier, and easier to detect.

items.title: Compilers can erase your security intent
items.oneliner: Black Hat researchers showed compiler optimizations can remove security checks. Source review is not enough; inspect the binary.

items.title: Google app install ads look polluted
items.oneliner: One developer found 60% of paid installs looked robotic. If you optimize for installs, expect bots to win.

items.title: Apple's Neural Engine looks transformer-obsolete
items.oneliner: A reverse-engineering deep dive says ANE was built for CNN dataflow. Transformer-era workloads are forcing hardware convergence.

items.title: LRU still wins KV cache reality
items.oneliner: Real agent-session simulations found fancy KV-cache policies could not beat LRU. Production caching remains stubbornly simple.

items.title: WebAssembly runtimes keep getting faster
items.oneliner: 2026 benchmarks show major WebAssembly runtime gains, with Wasmer leading speed tests. Portable compute keeps getting less theoretical.

items.title: SystemIO conflicts are usually not firmware bugs
items.oneliner: A Linux firmware expert says many ACPI SystemIO warnings reflect shared resource semantics, not broken firmware.
